## `arp4`

```text
ARP Rust: Excel, Word, PPTX and PDF document workflow

Usage: arp4 [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  spec       Build and validate evidence-backed specification models
  doctor
  skills
  documents
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version
```

## `arp4 spec`

```text
Build and validate evidence-backed specification models

Usage: arp4 spec [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  structure   Interpret original Excel structure without changing workbook contents or formatting
  workflow    Resume evidence-backed generation with pluggable model runners
  semantic    Prepare small semantic tasks and expand source-bound replies deterministically
  registry    Maintain canonical requirement/specification revisions and derived views
  assign-ids  Assign persistent sequential IDs using an explicit identity plan
  sources     Write complete source text in document/sheet/cell order
  schema      Save the full JSON Schema for extraction output
  capture     Capture parser extraction JSON files as a fixed input bundle
  prompt      Write the extraction and independent review instructions
  check
  render
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec structure`

```text
Interpret original Excel structure without changing workbook contents or formatting

Usage: arp4 spec structure [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  render  Render an element or visual's Excel range to PNG and register it as evidence. Requires Windows and desktop Excel; does not save changes to the workbook
  init    Create a read-only interpretation YAML from Excel, DOCX, PPTX or PDF extraction
  check   Validate source/image versions, cell references and review freshness
  read    Read the interpretation, original cells, compact drawings and verified image paths
  edit    Batch upsert/remove elements and visuals against the revision returned by read. Validate the whole interpretation and reset review only when content changes
  region  Register an existing PNG region on an element or visual; does not render Excel
  review  Record an actual review of this exact interpretation, including image hashes
  schema  Save the authoritative interpretation schema
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>
          Repository root used to verify original and image paths

          [default: .]

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec structure render`

```text
Render an element or visual's Excel range to PNG and register it as evidence. Requires Windows and desktop Excel; does not save changes to the workbook

Usage: arp4 spec structure render [OPTIONS] --extraction <EXTRACTION> --structure <STRUCTURE> --element <ELEMENT> --id <ID> --image <IMAGE>

Options:
      --extraction <EXTRACTION>


      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>
          Repository root used to verify original and image paths

          [default: .]

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --structure <STRUCTURE>


      --element <ELEMENT>


      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --id <ID>


      --image <IMAGE>
          New repository-relative PNG path outside disposable cache/work

      --range <RANGE>
          A1 range; omitted uses the visual's cell anchors, or the element sheet's UsedRange

      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          [default: 120]

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec workflow`

```text
Resume evidence-backed generation with pluggable model runners

Usage: arp4 spec workflow [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init
  status
  next            Read the next pending task without advancing state or invoking a model
  handoff         Prepare a compact worker assignment without reading task evidence or claiming it
  receipt         Confirm the latest recorded submission, including tasks retired after advance
  read            Read the complete task, automatically traversing nested data in bounded pages. Start without --pointer. Continue with page.next_command for your shell, keeping the same executable and workflow root/run-id prefix until page.complete
  validate-reply  Check a complete reply or draft correction without saving artifacts or history
  history         Inspect provider calls and external intervention history
  record-usage    Attach measured deltas to one external submission, including a retired task, or the cost of a provider run that recorded none. Existing measurements may be repeated identically, but never overwritten or added twice
  advance
  inspect
  submit          Submit a complete reply or a revision-bound draft correction; validate the whole result
  update
  run
  recover
  retry
  export
  compact
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>
          Repository root; otherwise discover .arp/config.yml within the Git boundary

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --run-id <RUN_ID>
          Local execution to resume (not a document version)

          [default: current]

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec workflow init`

```text
Usage: arp4 spec workflow init [OPTIONS] --input <INPUT>

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --review-plan <REVIEW_PLAN>
          JSON review plan with source IDs omitted from review and explicit reasons

      --input <INPUT>


      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --reply <REPLY>...


      --regions <REGIONS>


      --max-rounds <MAX_ROUNDS>
          Maximum repair/restructure waves for the entire run; then confirm and emit a draft if issues remain

          [default: 2]

      --review-granularity <REVIEW_GRANULARITY>
          Review unit selection. Adaptive batches small documents and splits large ones by sheet

          [default: adaptive]
          [possible values: adaptive, document, sheet]

      --modules <MODULES>
          Shared module slug/name vocabulary (JSON object)

      --extract-max-chars <EXTRACT_MAX_CHARS>
          Optional source-text character cap; zero disables it

          [default: 0]

      --extract-max-sources <EXTRACT_MAX_SOURCES>
          Optional source count cap; zero disables it

          [default: 0]

      --extract-max-bytes <EXTRACT_MAX_BYTES>
          UTF-8 task size, including instructions, schema and context

          [default: 98304]

      --reference <REFERENCE>...
          Reference text files (Markdown, plain text): supporting context for review and repair, readable with read --pointer references. Never a source

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec workflow read`

```text
Read the complete task, automatically traversing nested data in bounded pages. Start without --pointer. Continue with page.next_command for your shell, keeping the same executable and workflow root/run-id prefix until page.complete

Usage: arp4 spec workflow read [OPTIONS] --task <TASK>

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --task <TASK>


      --pointer <POINTER>
          [default: ""]

      --offset <OFFSET>
          [default: 0]

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Optional fragment count cap

          [default: 10000]

      --max-bytes <MAX_BYTES>
          Maximum reading response bytes (configured TOON or JSON). Lower for host truncation

          [default: 48000]

      --revision <REVISION>
          Copy page.revision when continuing; changed content requires restarting at offset 0

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec workflow record-usage`

```text
Attach measured deltas to one external submission, including a retired task, or the cost of a provider run that recorded none. Existing measurements may be repeated identically, but never overwritten or added twice

Usage: arp4 spec workflow record-usage [OPTIONS] --task <TASK> --usage-file <USAGE_FILE>

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --task <TASK>


      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --submission <SUBMISSION>
          One-based submission number within the task, as shown by history/receipt

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --run <RUN>
          One-based provider run number within the task, as shown by history. Only a run without a reported cost takes one; give --actor and --reason

      --usage-file <USAGE_FILE>
          Same measured usage JSON as submit --usage-file; no agent lifetime totals

      --actor <ACTOR>
          Who declares the cost of a provider run

      --reason <REASON>
          Where the declared cost comes from, such as the provider's billing record

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec workflow submit`

```text
Submit a complete reply or a revision-bound draft correction; validate the whole result

Usage: arp4 spec workflow submit [OPTIONS] --task <TASK>

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --task <TASK>


      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --reply <REPLY>


      --json <JSON>


      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --actor <ACTOR>
          [default: external]

      --model <MODEL>


      --reason <REASON>
          Short inline reason; defaults to "Externally supplied reply" when omitted

      --reason-file <REASON_FILE>
          Read the reason verbatim from a UTF-8 text file (optional BOM)

      --origin <ORIGIN>
          [default: external]
          [possible values: external, interactive-agent]

      --usage-file <USAGE_FILE>
          JSON with measured usage and reported_cost_usd; never estimates

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 spec workflow run`

```text
Usage: arp4 spec workflow run [OPTIONS] --provider <PROVIDER> --executable <EXECUTABLE> --model <MODEL>

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          [possible values: claude-code, command]

      --executable <EXECUTABLE>
          Absolute or relative path to the provider executable; no shell evaluation

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --arg <ARGUMENTS>
          Arguments for the command provider, repeated as --arg=value

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --model <MODEL>


      --max-calls <MAX_CALLS>
          [default: 1]

      --max-budget-usd <MAX_BUDGET_USD>
          Claude Code only; per-call budget, default 2 USD. Rejected by command provider

      --timeout <TIMEOUT>
          [default: 900]

      --extract-max-tokens <EXTRACT_MAX_TOKENS>
          [default: 16000]

      --repair-max-tokens <REPAIR_MAX_TOKENS>
          [default: 8000]

      --review-max-tokens <REVIEW_MAX_TOKENS>
          [default: 12000]

      --extract-effort <EXTRACT_EFFORT>
          [default: medium]
          [possible values: low, medium, high]

      --repair-effort <REPAIR_EFFORT>
          [default: adaptive]
          [possible values: adaptive, low, medium, high]

      --review-effort <REVIEW_EFFORT>
          [default: high]
          [possible values: low, medium, high]

      --total-budget-usd <TOTAL_BUDGET_USD>
          Total reported cost ceiling for this workflow (Claude only, including previous calls)

      --max-retries <MAX_RETRIES>
          Opt-in bounded recovery for transient failures or invalid replies, within max-calls

          [default: 0]

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents`

```text
Usage: arp4 documents [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  schema               Print a JSON contract by name, as a list of its properties; --pointer selects one node and --full prints all of it. An unknown name lists the contracts
  init                 Make the project's .arp folder and configuration
  import               Import an original, or every original below a folder, as proposals. The document ID is the original's path below the sources folder. Unchanged originals are skipped. An encrypted Office original is decrypted and saved over without its encryption first: a password with --password-stdin, IRM and sensitivity labels by desktop Office on Windows with the signed-in account's rights
  remove               Remove the documents at or below an ID whose originals were moved, renamed or deleted
  discard              Discard one proposal, leaving the original and adopted document untouched
  search               Search adopted extraction passages with Japanese segmentation, BM25 and source locations from the last explicitly refreshed local index
  search-formats       List the font colors, theme colors, fonts, sizes and emphasis of the indexed text, each with the hits a search filtering by it alone returns
  search-refresh       Reconcile canonical documents with the local search index
  structure-read       Write a derived structure view from the document's canonical corrections, with the report of how they replay on its extraction
  elements-read        Write the element metadata of every page, with current fonts resolved, and the visuals its references point to (the document-elements contract): the IDs, table rows and columns, headers, spans and formula kinds of the body
  extraction-read      Write the extraction for reading (the extraction-view contract): as extraction.json stores it, one cell per line, with each font and style written out where extraction.json has its index; a sheet gives the font and style most of its cells have once (cell_font, cell_style), and a cell only one of its own. A formula's cached result is its value
  structure-save       Save structure corrections; remove a managed work/structure view on success
  rows                 Insert or delete Excel worksheet rows, or Word and PowerPoint paragraphs and table rows. The operation in mappings.yml and the content values it adds or removes are written together, after the same validation as check
  columns              Insert or delete Excel worksheet columns, like rows
  cells                Insert or delete a range of Excel cells, shifting the cells beside it within its rows or columns, as Excel's Insert and Delete do. The insert_cells or delete_cells operation in mappings.yml and the content values it moves or removes are written together, after a trial write and the same validation as check: a value stays with its cell, shown at the row and column the cell ends in
  sheets               Add an empty Excel worksheet or a copy of one. The operation in mappings.yml, the sheet's content page (content/<name>.yml) and its layout are written together, after a trial write and the same validation as check
  slides               Copy, add, delete, move, hide or show PowerPoint slides. The operation in mappings.yml and the content pages it adds or removes are written together, after the same validation as check
  shapes               Change, add or delete shapes, pictures and connectors of a PowerPoint slide. Places and sizes are points on the slide, as the extraction's drawings give them; a shape is named by its drawing ID (<slide part>#<id>) or by the operation ID of the operation adding it
  images               Add PNG pictures to an Excel worksheet over a cell range. The operation in mappings.yml is written after a trial write and the same validation as check
  format               Change the format of a range of Excel cells: copy a cell's whole format (--from), alignment (--wrap, --shrink, --horizontal, --vertical), bold, italic, strike and underline, fill, borders, number format, row heights, column widths, or merge and take apart merges. The range names cells as the row and column operations recorded before leave them, as export writes them and layout_warnings names them; operations recorded after move it with the cells. Values stay. The format_cells operation in mappings.yml is written after a trial write and the same validation as check
  drawings             Move, resize or change the placement of Excel drawing objects. The place_drawing operation in mappings.yml is written after a trial write and the same validation as check
  links                Link Excel cells to places in the workbook or to URLs, or take their links off. The set_link or clear_links operation in mappings.yml names the cells as the row and column operations recorded before leave them; those recorded after move it with the cells. It is written last on export, after a trial write and the same validation as check
  notes                Give Excel cells notes, change their text or delete them, as set_note and clear_notes operations, placed and written like links
  validations          Give Excel cells data validations (drop-down lists, allowed values) or take them out of theirs, as set_validation and clear_validations operations, placed and written like links; rows and columns inserted after the cells later take them too, as in Excel
  conditional-formats  Add conditional formats to Excel cells or take them out of theirs, as add_conditional_format and clear_conditional_formats operations, placed and written like validations
  record               Record who formed a proposal, with which model and prompt. A folder ID or --all records every proposal below it that needs a record
  adopt                Adopt a recorded proposal as the document without marking it reviewed. A folder ID or --all adopts every proposal below it that is ready
  review               Review the edits of an adopted document. A folder ID or --all reviews every document below it that needs a review
  diff                 Show what changed: a proposal against its adopted document, or with --document an adopted document against the version Git's HEAD holds
  apply                Write the exact export candidate whose layout was confirmed to the original, then re-extract it as a proposal formed by apply, ready to adopt
  confirm-export       Record a human layout review of an exported candidate and its exact hash
  values               Edit values, formulas, table labels, shape texts and fonts of Office and PDF content, and give values to empty Excel cells, as the value-edits contract describes (documents schema value-edits). Targets are cells of the extraction or element IDs of elements-read, so the values of rows and slides operations insert are edited too. Every edit is checked, and written by the original's writer to a scratch file, before any is saved; the request is recorded with the content
  export               Without --out, plan the export of a reviewed document: what it writes to its original and what it leaves out. With --out, write the original with the edits to a new file and its report beside it
  render               Render a page of an exported candidate to a PNG image, to look at it before confirm-export: an Excel sheet or range, a Word or PDF page, or a PowerPoint slide. Needs Windows and desktop Office (Excel; Word or PowerPoint for their documents); PDF pages are rendered by Windows
  operations           List or take back pending row, column, slide, shape and image operations
  check                Check documents and proposals as edits leave them: their state, and the blockers or error keeping each from the next step. --include-hashes adds the content hash and the original's SHA-256 that value edits are based on
  status               The state of documents and proposals, like check
  help                 Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents search`

```text
Search adopted extraction passages with Japanese segmentation, BM25 and source locations from the last explicitly refreshed local index

Usage: arp4 documents search [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...

Arguments:
  [QUERY]...
          One to 32 quoted queries against one saved index snapshot. Within each query, whitespace separates literal AND terms; punctuation is not query syntax. With a format filter the query may be left out, to search by format alone. A format filter keeps a cell or shape text in the format in whole or in part

Options:
      --color <COLOR>
          Only hits with text in this font color: RRGGBB, a family (red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, purple, pink, gray, black, white), a theme slot (accent1, dk1, ...), auto, or mixed for text in several colors. Repeat for any of several

      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>


      --font <FONT>
          Only hits with text in this font, latin or East Asian, compared as search terms are. Repeat for any of several

      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --size <SIZE>
          Only hits with text in this size in points: N, N..M, N.. or ..M

      --bold
          Only hits with bold text

      --italic
          Only hits with italic text

      --underline
          Only hits with underlined text, in any line

      --strike
          Only hits with struck-through text, by one line or two

      --highlight
          Only hits with highlighted text (Word and PowerPoint)

      --fill
          Only hits with text in a filled cell (Excel cells, Word table cells)

      --document <DOCUMENT>
          Restrict to a document ID or folder ID

      --synonyms <SYNONYMS>
          Project vocabulary groups (search-synonyms schema). Defaults to .arp/search-synonyms.yml if present

      --profile
          Emit disjoint search wall-clock timings as one JSON record on stderr

      --revision <REVISION>
          Pin pagination to a previous index and query revision

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text
  move    Excel only: move rows of the original sheet to the place --after or --before names, as Excel inserts cut rows: recorded as rows inserted there with the formats, heights and merges of the rows moved (<id>-insert), their values and formulas copied there (<id>-copy), their links, notes, validations and drawings set there, and the rows deleted (<id>-delete); the formulas reading the rows, there or elsewhere, are given the text Excel gives them, and the formats recorded on the rows recorded where they go. A move Excel would make otherwise is refused: one with names whose ends move, rules over only the rows or only the place they go to, or drawings over the rows and others
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:

          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents rows insert`

```text
Insert rows and write their values under the keys <operation ID>-<n>

Usage: arp4 documents rows insert [OPTIONS] --sheet <SHEET> --reason <REASON> <--after <AFTER>|--before <BEFORE>> [DOCUMENT]

Arguments:
  [DOCUMENT]
          Adopted document ID

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --proposal <PROPOSAL>
          Edit the proposal of this document ID instead, before record

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --sheet <SHEET>
          Worksheet name; for Word the part (document, header-N, ...), for PowerPoint the page (slide-N, notes-N, or the operation ID of an inserted slide)

      --id <ID>
          Operation ID (^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$); generated when omitted. Give one so that repeating the command, e.g. after a timeout, is reported unchanged

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --reason <REASON>
          Why the rows or columns change; recorded with the operation

      --base <BASE>
          The content hash from check --include-hashes; the edit is refused when the document changed since

      --dry-run
          Validate and report the edit without writing

      --vba-unchanged
          Excel workbooks with a VBA project: accept that the edit leaves the cell addresses in the VBA code as they are, as Excel does. Give it only after a person checked the macros against the lines vba_not_updated lists; it is recorded with the operation

      --after <AFTER>
          Insert after this row or column: a row number (15 or r15) or column letters (C) of the original sheet, the key <operation ID>-<n> of one an earlier operation inserted, or last (the last one holding a value)

      --before <BEFORE>
          Insert before this row or column, given like --after

      --count <COUNT>
          Number of rows; defaults to the number of --values items, or 1

      --style-from <STYLE_FROM>
          Original row whose formatting the new rows take; defaults to the row above them, as in Excel. Excel rows `9:10` are taken in turn by each group of new rows, as a form laid out over two rows

      --merges
          Excel only: make the merges within the style rows (--style-from, by default the row above) again over each group of new rows, as Excel's Insert Copied Cells does

      --values <VALUES>
          YAML or JSON file, or - for stdin: a list with one object per new row, keyed by column letter, e.g. [{B: "8", C: 2025/11/21}]. Values take the type of the column (the --style-from row, or the nearest value above)

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents cells`

```text
Insert or delete a range of Excel cells, shifting the cells beside it within its rows or columns, as Excel's Insert and Delete do. The insert_cells or delete_cells operation in mappings.yml and the content values it moves or removes are written together, after a trial write and the same validation as check: a value stays with its cell, shown at the row and column the cell ends in

Usage: arp4 documents cells [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  insert  Insert empty cells over the range, shifting the cells there and below it down (--shift down) or right of it right (--shift right) within the range's columns or rows. The new cells take the format of the cell above or left of them, as in Excel, and take values with documents values set or in the content
  delete  Delete the cells of the range with their values, shifting the cells below it up (--shift up) or right of it left (--shift left) within the range's columns or rows
  copy    Copy the cells of the range to the place at --to of the same sheet, as Excel pastes them: the values and formulas, their relative references moved by the distance, as value edits, and the formats and merges as a copy_cells operation, written together. The cells pasted over holding a value a formula would replace, or a formula, are refused
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text
Usage: arp4 documents cells insert [OPTIONS] --sheet <SHEET> --range <RANGE> --reason <REASON> --shift <SHIFT> [DOCUMENT]
```

## `arp4 documents sheets`

```text
Add an empty Excel worksheet or a copy of one. The operation in mappings.yml, the sheet's content page (content/<name>.yml) and its layout are written together, after a trial write and the same validation as check

Usage: arp4 documents sheets [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:

  copy    Copy a worksheet of the original, as Excel's Move or Copy with Create a copy does: cells, formats, rows and columns, merges, rules, links, notes, drawings, charts, tables and print settings. Refused for sheets with pivot tables, threaded comments, controls or embedded objects, and for sheets with row, column or cell operations recorded: copy the sheet first
  delete  Delete a worksheet of the original, as Excel deletes a sheet: formulas, rules, chart series and names naming it read #REF!, its own names go, links are left as they are. Its content page goes with the operations and value edits recorded on it (dropped_operations). Export deletes it after every other edit. Refused for the last visible sheet and a sheet a pivot table reads from
  rename  Rename a worksheet of the original, as Excel renames a sheet: formulas, rules, chart series and names naming it name it so, links are left as they are. Export renames it after every other edit, so the other commands keep naming it by its name in the original
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
```

## `arp4 documents slides`

```text
Copy, add, delete, move, hide or show PowerPoint slides. The operation in mappings.yml and the content pages it adds or removes are written together, after the same validation as check

Usage: arp4 documents slides [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  insert  Insert a copy of a slide and its notes page, as PowerPoint's Duplicate Slide does, with their text in new content pages named by the operation ID (content/<ID>.yml, content/notes-<ID>.yml). Comments are not copied
  add     Add a new slide made from a slide layout, as PowerPoint's New Slide does: one empty placeholder for each of the layout's placeholders (but date, footer and slide number), whose text is written in the new content page named by the operation ID (content/<ID>.yml)
  delete  Delete a slide of the original with its notes page and their content pages. Refused while another slide links to it
  move    Move a slide, with its notes page, next to another slide in the show order. In a presentation with sections it joins the other slide's section. Custom shows keep their own order
  hide    Hide a slide from the slide show; it stays in the presentation
  show    Show a hidden slide in the slide show again
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents shapes`

```text
Change, add or delete shapes, pictures and connectors of a PowerPoint slide. Places and sizes are points on the slide, as the extraction's drawings give them; a shape is named by its drawing ID (<slide part>#<id>) or by the operation ID of the operation adding it

Usage: arp4 documents shapes [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  update           Change the place, size, rotation, fill, line or name of a shape, picture, connector, group or table frame. Unset properties stay as they are
  add              Add a rectangle, rounded rectangle, ellipse, text box or line, with PowerPoint's default shape style unless --fill and --line are given
  delete           Delete a shape, picture, connector or group without text. A shape showing the slide's text or joined by a connector is refused
  add-picture      Add a PNG picture from the document's assets folder
  replace-picture  Show another PNG picture in a picture, keeping its place and size
  add-connector    Add a connector joining two shapes at connection sites: a rectangle's are 0 top, 1 left, 2 bottom and 3 right; an ellipse's 0 top to 7, counterclockwise every 45 degrees
  help             Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents format`

```text
Change the format of a range of Excel cells: copy a cell's whole format (--from), alignment (--wrap, --shrink, --horizontal, --vertical), bold, italic, strike and underline, fill, borders, number format, row heights, column widths, or merge and take apart merges. The range names cells as the row and column operations recorded before leave them, as export writes them and layout_warnings names them; operations recorded after move it with the cells. Values stay. The format_cells operation in mappings.yml is written after a trial write and the same validation as check

Usage: arp4 documents format [OPTIONS] --sheet <SHEET> --range <RANGE> --reason <REASON> [DOCUMENT]

Arguments:
  [DOCUMENT]
          Adopted document ID of an Excel workbook

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --proposal <PROPOSAL>
          Edit the proposal of this document ID instead, before record

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --sheet <SHEET>
          Worksheet of the original

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --range <RANGE>
          The cells, such as B3:F10 or B3

      --from <FROM>
          Cell whose whole format (borders, fill, number format, font, alignment) the range takes

      --wrap <WRAP>
          Wrap text in the cells (true) or not (false)

          [possible values: true, false]

      --shrink <SHRINK>
          Shrink text to fit the cells (true) or not (false)

          [possible values: true, false]

      --horizontal <HORIZONTAL>
          Horizontal alignment

          [possible values: general, left, center, right, fill, justify, centerContinuous, distributed]

      --vertical <VERTICAL>
          Vertical alignment

          [possible values: top, center, bottom, justify, distributed]

      --bold <BOLD>
          Make the text bold (true) or not (false)

          [possible values: true, false]

      --italic <ITALIC>
          Make the text italic (true) or not (false)

          [possible values: true, false]

      --strike <STRIKE>
          Strike the text through (true) or not (false)

          [possible values: true, false]

      --underline <UNDERLINE>
          Underline the text

          [possible values: none, single, double]

      --fill <FILL>
          Fill the cells with a solid color, RRGGBB, or none for no fill

      --number-format <NUMBER_FORMAT>
          Number format code, such as 0.00, #,##0, yyyy/mm/dd or @ (text)

      --border <BORDERS>
          Lines to draw, as edges:style[:RRGGBB], applied in the order given: edges all, outline, inside, horizontal, vertical, top, bottom, left or right of the range; style thin, medium, thick, dashed, dotted, double, hair, ... or none to take the lines away. Repeat for more

      --row-height <ROW_HEIGHT>
          Height of the range's rows in points, or auto for the height Excel fits to their text on opening

      --column-width <COLUMN_WIDTH>
          Width of the range's columns in characters, as Excel gives it

      --merge
          Merge the range; its cells other than the top left must be empty

      --unmerge
          Take apart the merged ranges inside the range

      --id <ID>
          Operation ID (^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$); generated when omitted

      --reason <REASON>
          Why the format changes; recorded with the operation

      --base <BASE>
          The content hash from check --include-hashes; the edit is refused when the document changed since

      --dry-run
          Validate and report the edit without writing

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents links`

```text
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)
```

```text
      --sheet <SHEET>
          Worksheet of the original

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --range <RANGE>
          The cells, such as B3:F10 or B3, as the row and column operations recorded before leave them, as export writes them

          [alias: --cell]

      --id <ID>
          Operation ID (^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*$); generated when omitted

      --reason <REASON>
          Why the cells change; recorded with the operation

      --base <BASE>
          The content hash from check --include-hashes; the edit is refused when the document changed since

      --dry-run
          Validate and report the edit without writing

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text

  [DOCUMENT]

          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)
```

```text
      --dry-run
          List the documents this would take and those it skips, without writing

          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --out <OUT>
          With --dry-run, save the plan to this new file for --expect

      --expect <EXPECT>
          A plan saved by --dry-run --out: take only the documents it lists, and only while their content is the one it lists

      --model <MODEL>


      --actor <ACTOR>


      --prompt <PROMPT>
```


```text
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

## `arp4 documents values`

```text
Edit values, formulas, table labels, shape texts and fonts of Office and PDF content, and give values to empty Excel cells, as the value-edits contract describes (documents schema value-edits). Targets are cells of the extraction or element IDs of elements-read, so the values of rows and slides operations insert are edited too. Every edit is checked, and written by the original's writer to a scratch file, before any is saved; the request is recorded with the content

Usage: arp4 documents values [OPTIONS] --input <INPUT> [DOCUMENT]

Arguments:
  [DOCUMENT]
          Adopted document ID

Options:
      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --proposal <PROPOSAL>
          Edit the proposal of this document ID instead, before record

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --input <INPUT>
          The value-edits request, a JSON or YAML file, or - for stdin. Its base and source_sha256 come from check --include-hashes

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --dry-run
          Validate and report the edits without writing

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text
  <DOCUMENT>

      --include-hashes

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```

```text
Usage: arp4 documents render [OPTIONS] --candidate <CANDIDATE> --out <OUT> <DOCUMENT>

Arguments:
  <DOCUMENT>


Options:
      --candidate <CANDIDATE>
          The exported file, beside its .report.json

      --full
          Return all details (not supported by spec workflow; use read pagination there)

      --root <ROOT>


      --include-hashes
          Include verification hashes in output: the content hash and the original's SHA-256 in check and status, and those of edits, reviews and exports

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --out <OUT>
          New PNG file to write

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

      --sheet <SHEET>
          Excel worksheet to render

      --range <RANGE>
          Excel A1 range; the sheet's used range when omitted

      --page <PAGE>
          Page of a Word or PDF document, or slide of a presentation in the candidate's order, from 1

          [default: 120]

          Print help
```

```text
  remove  Take back a pending operation with what it did to the content: the values of rows, columns and slides it inserted leave the content, and those it deleted come back as the original holds them.       --limit <LIMIT>
          Maximum items per page (default: 20)

      --offset <OFFSET>
          Zero-based item offset (default: 0); use page.next_offset for the next page

  -h, --help
          Print help
```
